title: Soft Bakery-Style Pumpkin Muffins
excerpt: When the mornings turn crisp and the kitchen fills with the cozy scent of cinnamon, these soft pumpkin muffins feel like a little celebration. They are tender, warmly spiced, and just right for a family breakfast during Halloween week, especially with a sparkling cinnamon sugar top.

Why You'll Love This Pumpkin Muffins

  • These pumpkin muffins are soft, tender, and full of cozy cinnamon spice.
  • A sparkling cinnamon sugar topping adds a lovely little crunch to every bite.
  • The batter comes together quickly with simple pantry ingredients.
  • They are perfect for Halloween week breakfasts, lunchboxes, or an afternoon treat.
  • Each batch makes 12 generous muffins for sharing with family and friends.

Ingredients

Gather these simple ingredients before you begin, and your kitchen will soon smell like a warm autumn morning.

  • All-purpose flour - 1 3/4 cups
  • Baking soda - 1 teaspoon
  • Baking powder - 1/2 teaspoon
  • Salt - 1/2 teaspoon
  • Ground cinnamon - 1 1/2 teaspoons
  • Ground ginger - 1/2 teaspoon
  • Ground nutmeg - 1/4 teaspoon
  • Large eggs - 2
  • Pumpkin puree - 1 cup
  • Packed light brown sugar - 3/4 cup
  • Vegetable oil - 1/2 cup
  • Milk - 1/4 cup
  • Granulated sugar - 2 tablespoons, for topping
  • Ground cinnamon - 1/2 teaspoon, for topping

How to Make Pumpkin Muffins

Plan on 15 minutes of prep and 18 to 22 minutes of baking, with 5 minutes of cooling in the pan before the muffins move to a rack.

Step 1: Preheat the Oven

Preheat the oven to 375°F. A fully heated oven helps the muffins rise nicely from the very start.

Step 2: Line the Pan

Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners. This keeps the muffins easy to lift out and makes cleanup pleasantly simple.

Step 3: Whisk the Dry Ingredients

Whisk the flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt, cinnamon, ginger, and nutmeg in a medium bowl. Mixing them first helps distribute the leavening and spices evenly.

Step 4: Whisk the Wet Ingredients

Whisk the eggs, pumpkin puree, brown sugar, oil, and milk in a large bowl until smooth. The pumpkin mixture should look evenly blended before the dry ingredients are added.

Step 5: Combine the Batter

Fold the dry ingredients into the pumpkin mixture until just combined. Stop mixing as soon as you no longer see dry streaks to keep the muffins tender.

Step 6: Fill the Muffin Cups

Divide the batter evenly among the muffin cups. Filling them evenly helps all 12 muffins finish baking at about the same time.

Step 7: Mix the Topping

Stir the granulated sugar and cinnamon together in a small bowl. This quick mixture will give the tops a sweet, gently crisp finish.

Step 8: Sprinkle the Topping

Sprinkle the cinnamon sugar over the batter. Try to divide it evenly so every muffin gets a little sparkle.

Step 9: Bake the Muffins

Bake the muffins for 18 to 22 minutes. They are ready when the tops look set and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean or with a few moist crumbs.

Step 10: Cool in the Pan

Cool the muffins in the pan for 5 minutes. This short rest lets them firm up gently without becoming difficult to remove.

Step 11: Transfer to a Rack

Transfer the muffins to a wire rack to cool. Serve them warm or let them cool completely before storing.

Pro Tips for Making Pumpkin Muffins

  • Use pumpkin puree rather than pumpkin pie filling, since the recipe already includes its own sugar and spices.
  • Measure the flour by spooning it into a measuring cup and leveling the top for a lighter muffin.
  • Fold the batter gently and stop as soon as the ingredients are combined. A few small lumps are fine.
  • For evenly sized muffins, use a scoop or spoon to portion the batter between the liners.
  • Let the muffins cool slightly before serving so the centers have time to settle.

How to Serve Pumpkin Muffins

  • Serve warm with a pat of butter or a spoonful of plain yogurt.
  • Pair one with scrambled eggs and fresh fruit for a cozy breakfast.
  • Pack them in lunchboxes once completely cooled.
  • Arrange them on a family-style platter for a Halloween week breakfast.

Make Ahead and Storage

Storing Leftovers

  • Cool the muffins completely before storing them in an airtight container.
  • Keep them at room temperature for up to 3 days.
  • Place a paper towel under and over the muffins to help absorb excess moisture.

Freezing

  • Wrap completely cooled muffins individually or place them in a freezer-safe container.
  • Freeze for up to 2 months for the best texture.
  • Thaw the muffins at room temperature before serving.

Reheating

  • Warm one muffin in the microwave for 10 to 15 seconds.
  • For several muffins, place them in a low oven until gently warmed.
  • Do not overheat, as this can dry out the tender crumb.

Final Thoughts

These soft pumpkin muffins bring a little bakery-style comfort to the breakfast table, one warmly spiced bite at a time.

FAQs

Here are a few helpful answers for making and enjoying this cozy batch of pumpkin muffins.

Can I use homemade pumpkin puree?

Yes, homemade pumpkin puree works well as long as it is smooth and not overly watery. If it seems loose, drain off a little excess liquid before measuring.

Why are my pumpkin muffins dense?

Dense muffins are often caused by overmixing the batter or measuring too much flour. Fold just until combined and measure the flour carefully.

Can I make these pumpkin muffins without paper liners?

Yes, lightly grease the muffin pan before adding the batter. Let the muffins cool for a few minutes so they release more easily.

How do I know when the muffins are done?

Insert a toothpick into the center of a muffin. It should come out clean or with a few moist crumbs, and the tops should look set.
